description: LNG carrier, gas carrier and tanker thickness measurement at Ras Laffan: hull structure, ballast tank and pre-docking gauging for renewal surveys.
h1: Thickness Measurement for LNG Carriers and Gas Ships at Ras Laffan
intro: Ras Laffan, on Qatar's north-east coast, is one of the largest LNG export ports in the world, and the Erhama Bin Jaber Al Jalahma Shipyard inside the port docks gas carriers, tankers and other large ships. For superintendents running LNG, LPG and condensate ships, we provide thickness measurement at Ras Laffan for renewal and docking surveys, pre-docking steel estimates and condition records. Technicians travel from India, and their passes for the port's strict entry controls are arranged before they fly.

highlights.h: TM plans sized for Q-Max hulls
highlights.p: The largest ships in the Qatari LNG fleet carry very large ballast tank areas and long trunk decks. A compartment-by-compartment plan agreed before docking keeps the reading count manageable without missing the areas class requires.

highlights.h: Docking periods at the port yard
highlights.p: Gas carriers trading from Ras Laffan can dock at the shipyard inside the port without a long positioning voyage. That is where full renewal-survey gauging and post-repair confirmation readings are done.

highlights.h: Steam plants and big seawater systems
highlights.p: Steam-turbine LNG carriers run large main condenser seawater circuits. Warm Gulf intake water speeds internal wastage in those lines, sea chests and the fire main, so piping deserves a place in the plan.

port.h: Ras Laffan: Qatar's LNG export port and its gas fleet
p: Ras Laffan Industrial City, on the north-east coast of the Qatar peninsula, is built around the liquefaction trains that process gas from the offshore North Field. Its port loads LNG for buyers in Asia, Europe and beyond, alongside LPG, condensate, refined products and the gas-to-liquids products of the Pearl and Oryx GTL plants. The fleet that calls is specialised and valuable: membrane and Moss-type LNG carriers, including the large Q-Flex and Q-Max designs developed for the Qatari trade, plus LPG carriers, condensate tankers and product tankers.

LNG carriers turn round quickly at the loading berths, so the port stay itself rarely allows gauging beyond a few accessible spaces. Time comes at the shipyard. The Erhama Bin Jaber Al Jalahma Shipyard, inside the port limits, was built to take the largest LNG carriers in the Qatari fleet and handles repair, docking and survey work for gas carriers, tankers and offshore units. Its location means ships trading from Ras Laffan can dock without a long ballast passage to a distant yard. Ships also wait at the Ras Laffan anchorage for loading slots, which can open short windows for deck and ballast-tank work on LPG carriers and tankers.

Gauging demand at Ras Laffan is therefore centred on docking periods. LNG carriers are surveyed against IACS UR Z7, the general hull survey requirement, together with the class society's gas-carrier rules, rather than the ESP regime, so the gauging extent differs from a crude tanker's. The cargo containment itself is not the target; the work is on the hull envelope, the inner hull measured from within the ballast tanks, double-bottom and wing ballast tanks, cofferdams, trunk deck and weather deck, and the ship's seawater, ballast and fire-main piping. Older steam-turbine LNG carriers coming to the end of long charters add pre-sale and pre-conversion gauging to the mix, where a buyer wants measured margins rather than the seller's maintenance history.

facilities.h: Where LNG carrier hull gauging is done at Ras Laffan
p: Most full programmes take place at the Erhama Bin Jaber Al Jalahma Shipyard, where ships are in dry dock or at repair berths with staging and gas-free certificates in place. The yard's sequence drives the work: ballast tanks are opened, cleaned and ventilated in groups, so we take readings tank by tank as they are released and pass suspect results to the superintendent each day. On membrane ships, readings on the inner hull are taken from the ballast side only, and nothing is done inside the cargo containment system.

Outside the yard, opportunities are limited but real. LPG carriers, condensate tankers and product tankers sometimes have idle periods at anchorage or lay-by, when deck plating, accessible ballast tanks and piping can be measured. Port service craft, the tugs, mooring launches and pilot boats that work the LNG berths, also need gauging at their renewal surveys. Because every visit to the industrial city depends on security passes, we try to group these smaller scopes with a docking already planned at the yard, so the permits and travel serve more than one vessel.
list: Erhama Bin Jaber Al Jalahma Shipyard — renewal and docking-survey gauging on LNG carriers, LPG carriers and tankers in dry dock, with confirmation readings after steel renewal
Shipyard repair berths — afloat gauging of ballast tanks, cofferdams and piping on gas carriers before the ship enters dock or after it floats out
Ras Laffan anchorage — deck, ballast tank and piping checks on LPG carriers and product tankers waiting for loading slots, by launch through the agent
Condensate and product berths — limited pipe and deck gauging on tankers lying idle at the berth, subject to the terminal's own permit
Port service craft berths — renewal-survey gauging of the tugs, mooring launches and pilot boats that handle the LNG fleet

context.h: Gas-carrier rules, port state control and the LNG expansion
p: Ras Laffan is a Qatari port and so is covered by the Riyadh MoU port state control regime, though the LNG fleet calling here also faces demanding charterer and terminal vetting. Gas carriers are inspected under OCIMF's SIRE programme like oil and chemical tankers, and terminal acceptance depends on a clean record. No emission control area applies in Qatari waters. LNG carriers burn boil-off gas for much of their propulsion, so scrubber piping is rarely the issue here, but large seawater systems are, particularly on steam-turbine ships with big main condenser circuits drawing warm Gulf water.

QatarEnergy's North Field expansion is adding liquefaction capacity at Ras Laffan and has brought a large new fleet of LNG carriers into service, with more to follow. For new ships, an owner-specified baseline of readings at an early docking gives every later survey a reference. At the other end of the age range, steam-turbine LNG carriers built for the early Qatari contracts are reaching the point where owners choose between further trading, conversion to floating storage or regasification units, or sale, and each option calls for a clear picture of the hull's remaining margins. Warm, saline ballast water and high deck temperatures work against the coatings in wing and double-bottom tanks on all of them.

jobs.h: Typical gauging jobs at Ras Laffan
jobs.p: Ras Laffan work almost always follows a docking or a commercial decision about a gas carrier. The scopes below show the usual pattern. Each is planned from the class survey status, the previous gauging records and the yard's work sequence, and gauging is coordinated with the superintendent so suspect areas reach the repair list before the dock period runs out.
list: Renewal-survey gauging of a membrane LNG carrier at the Erhama yard: wing and double-bottom ballast tanks, the ballast-side face of the inner hull, cofferdams, trunk deck and side shell.
Ballast tank gauging on LNG carriers ahead of docking, carried out at the yard's repair berth so the owner can firm up steel renewal before the dock date.
Main condenser seawater circulating lines, sea chests and fire main gauging on a steam-turbine LNG carrier, where warm Gulf intake water speeds up internal wastage.
Pre-sale condition gauging of an older Moss-type LNG carrier offered for conversion to floating storage, giving the buyer a measured record of the hull.
LPG carrier thickness measurement during a docking: ballast tanks, hold spaces around the cargo tanks, deck and piping, scoped to the class renewal survey.

logistics: Hamad International Airport (DOH) is the arrival point, served directly from many Indian cities, and from there the team drives north to Ras Laffan Industrial City. Entry to the industrial city and the port is tightly controlled: every person needs a security pass applied for in advance, sponsored through the yard or the ship's agent, and the portable gauging equipment may also need to be declared. Entry formalities for Qatar are handled ahead of travel, which is why we want the docking date as early as possible and start the pass applications alongside them.

faqs.q: Do you gauge inside the cargo tanks of membrane LNG carriers?
faqs.a: No. Membrane containment systems are inspected by specialists under the containment designer's and the class society's procedures, and they are not part of an ultrasonic hull gauging scope. Our work covers the hull structure around them: the inner hull as reached from the ballast tanks, the ballast tanks themselves, cofferdams, trunk deck, weather deck and shell plating, plus the ship's piping systems.

faqs.q: How does gas carrier thickness gauging differ from tanker gauging?
faqs.a: Gas carriers are not covered by the ESP Code, so the extent of measurement comes from IACS UR Z7 plus the gas-carrier rules of the ship's classification society, not the UR Z10 series. In practice the focus shifts to ballast tanks, cofferdams and the hull envelope around the cargo tanks, with fewer readings in cargo spaces. The ship's age and the renewal survey number still drive the extent.

faqs.q: What permits are needed for ultrasonic thickness measurement at Ras Laffan?
faqs.a: Each technician needs a Ras Laffan security pass, and the portable equipment being brought in may also have to be registered. Inside the yard, tank entry follows the yard's permit-to-work and gas-free certification system. Because pass approvals take time, we ask for the docking date, the yard contact and the agent's details as soon as the docking is booked.

faqs.q: Is gauging useful on a new LNG carrier that has only just entered service?
faqs.a: It can be. A newbuild has no history, and a measured baseline of key areas, such as ballast tank plating and stiffeners, deck, bottom and side shell, at an early docking gives later surveys a reference against original thicknesses. For owners of large new fleets, consistent baseline data across sister ships also makes it easier to spot a ship or a tank that is wearing faster than the rest.
